title: One Is Not Enough: How People Use Multiple AI Models in Everyday Life
abstract: arXiv:2603.26107v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: People increasingly use multiple Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) concurrently, selecting each based on its perceived strengths. This cross-platform practice creates coordination challenges: adapting prompts to different interfaces, calibrating trust against inconsistent behaviors, and navigating separate conversation histories. Prior HCI research focused on single-agent interactions, leaving multi-MLLM orchestration underexplored. Through a diary study and semi-structured interviews (N=10), we examine how individuals organize work across competing AI systems. Our findings reveal that users construct primary and secondary hierarchies among models that shift over usage context. They also develop personalized switching patterns triggered by task aggregation to adjust effort and latency, and output credibility. These insights inform future tool design opportunities, supporting users to coordinate multi-MLLM workflows.

translated_title: 一个还不够：人们如何在日常生活中使用多个AI模型
translated_abstract: 人们越来越多地同时使用多个多模态大语言模型（MLLM），并根据各自感知到的优势进行选择。这种跨平台的使用方式带来了协调上的挑战：需要针对不同界面调整提示词、针对模型间不一致的表现校准信任度，以及管理相互分离的对话历史。以往的人机交互（HCI）研究主要聚焦于单智能体交互，对多模型协同编排的探索尚不充分。通过日记研究和半结构化访谈（N=10），我们考察了个体如何在相互竞争的AI系统之间组织工作。研究结果表明，用户会在不同模型之间构建主次层级关系，且这种层级会随使用情境而变化。用户还发展出个性化的切换模式，由任务聚合触发，用以调节投入精力、响应延迟和输出可信度。这些见解为未来的工具设计指明了方向，以支持用户协调多模型工作流。
tldr: 本研究通过日记研究与访谈揭示了用户如何在多个AI模型之间建立主次层级并形成个性化的切换模式，为设计支持多模型协同工作流的工具提供了启示。
en_tdlr: Through a diary study and interviews (N=10), this paper reveals how users establish primary-secondary hierarchies among multiple AI models and develop personalized switching patterns, informing the design of tools that support multi-LLM workflow orchestration.
